title: moonbuggy survivor-export record (C3 Phase A findings feed)
description: One machine-readable finding record exported from a moonbuggy run: a single JSON object per line, one line per SURVIVED or NO_COVERAGE mutant. Each line reuses the record-schema-4 JSONL envelope verbatim (the same field set results.jsonl carries, including original/mutated/diff/nearest_test and killreason) under a survivor-export version pin, so a reader with one line can reconstruct the mutant and re-inject it via `moonbuggy run <id>`. A change that adds, renames, or re-types a key raises the schema version rather than silently shifting the contract. `survival_reason` is deliberately null in v1: the survival-reason vocabulary is C3 Phase B and does not exist yet -- no token may be invented here.

schema.description: Version of the survivor-export contract. Every conforming record carries it so a reader with one line knows exactly what that line means.

exported.description: When the export was produced, UTC.

moonbuggy.description: moonbuggy __version__ of the tree that ran the source run and wrote this export.

record_schema.description: The RECORD_SCHEMA version of the embedded finding fields. The export carries the record envelope verbatim, so the envelope's own version travels with it rather than being inferred.

survival_reason.description: Why this mutant survived. NOT YET IN VOCABULARY: the stable survival-reason tokens are C3 Phase B and are intentionally absent from v1 -- this field is reserved, required, and always null. A Phase B version bump widens the type to include the new tokens; no v1 consumer may interpret null as any reason.

id.description: The mutant id, as printed in `id=...` on a result line. This is the re-injection handle: `moonbuggy run <id>` accepts it directly.

status.description: The finding verdict. The export is findings-only: killed, timed-out, suspicious and skipped mutants are never exported.

file.description: The mutated module, relative to the project root.

operator.description: The mutation operator that produced the mutant.

category.description: The record's category token (currently the operator name, carried verbatim from the record envelope).

nearest_test.description: The test node id nearest to the mutated line, or None when the run recorded no neighbour.

tests_run.description: How many selected tests ran against the mutant.

duration.description: The mutant's measured wall time in seconds, as the record carries it.

module_level.description: Whether the mutation sits on an import-time line.

suppressed.description: Whether the mutant was settled without running (skip marker or suppressed logging mutant). Carried verbatim for provenance; a suppressed mutant is not a genuine finding.

logging_call.description: Whether the mutation sits inside a logging call's arguments.

diff.description: The two-line textual diff (`- original` / `+ mutated`), exactly as the record envelope renders it.

accepted.description: Whether the accepted-equivalents ledger covers this mutant. An accepted survivor is annotated, never hidden: it still exports, with the ledger's verdict alongside.

accept_reason.description: The ledger's reason for accepting this mutant, or None when it is not accepted.

killreason.description: A killreason token from the frozen D1 vocabulary, or null. A finding record always carries null -- killreason is a cause of a kill, and no finding was killed -- but the field travels verbatim so a consumer may treat exported lines and results.jsonl lines with one parser.
